chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Playing with Louis Armstrong at the Vendome; Jabbo Smith
summary: Wilson filled in for two weeks in Tate's pit with Armstrong, and recalls Jabbo Smith challenging Louis at the Sunset.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: He was in Louis Armstrong-or Carroll Dickerson's band at the Sunset.
You ever hear that band out there?
You kidding? That's when I used to chin myself up to the window. I was in short pants then.
Well, I worked with Louis at the Met. No, at the Vendome Theater.
Oh, really? Whose band was that?
He was a member of the band, and I filled in two weeks for the bass player. But Louis was a member of Erskine Tate's band, playing in the pit.
That was -- Armstrong, you know, just judging by the recordings from that time, was marvelous.
Were the guys really -- were they aware that he was as great as we know him today?
No, I don't think so. Not in them days.
He was just another one of the good players around?
He was just a good trumpet player, you know. He wasn't famous as he was -- as he got in later years, you know.
Was Jabbo Smith around town then?
Yeah. Jabbo used to come to the Sunset and challenge you.
The only man that I know that challenged Louie was Jabbo Smith.
Hard to say. Because Jabbo was a tough man, too.
Very fast in those days. Did you play any with Jabbo?
Yeah, Jabbo worked with me up in Milwaukee in later years. Still . . . . the Wisconsin Roof Garden.
Yeah, that was with Floyd Campbell's band.
I don't know. Don't remember the year.
